checklist.criterion: Context section states the prior problem: Explains concretely what was wrong with hand-written checks before Zod (inconsistency, drift, or similar), not a vague statement
Decision section is specific: States that Zod is adopted for boundary validation and that types are derived via `z.infer`, not a vague "we use a validation library"
At least two real alternatives with reasons: Lists two or more concrete alternatives (e.g. hand-written predicates, Yup, io-ts) each with a specific reason it wasn't chosen
Consequences include at least one real cost: States a cost accepted by the decision (dependency weight, learning curve, migration effort), not only benefits
Standard ADR structure is followed: Includes Title, Status, Context, Decision, Alternatives Considered, and Consequences as identifiable sections
